# Reference: Security Model

---
sidebar_position: 5
title: Security Model
description: Capability-based authority, policy confinement, information-flow labels, contract verification bounds, and supply-chain provenance in AILANG.
reviewed: 2026-11-26
reviewBy: 2027-05-26
---

# AILANG Security Model

AILANG enforces **explicit authority** at the language and runtime boundary: side effects must appear in function types (`! {IO, FS, ...}`), and capabilities must be granted when running a program. However, **AILANG is not an OS sandbox** — capabilities like `FS`, `Process`, and `Env` grant broad host access unless narrowed by `AILANG_FS_SANDBOX`, `--policy` (Experimental), or OS-level isolation (containers, VMs, seccomp).

---

## Capabilities (`--caps`)

Every value accepted by `ailang run --caps` corresponds to a runtime capability. Capabilities marked **Stable** belong to Stable stdlib modules; **Experimental** capabilities belong to Experimental modules and may evolve in `1.x` minors (see [Stability Promise](/docs/reference/stability)).

| Capability | Tier | What it grants at runtime |
|---|---|---|
| `IO` | Stable | Console stdout/stderr/stdin (`print`, `println`, `readLine`, `readLineOpt`, `exit`) and `std/terminal` TTY control |
| `FS` | Stable | Read, write, mkdir, rename, walk, and delete across every host path the OS user can reach, unless narrowed by `AILANG_FS_SANDBOX` or `--policy` (`fs_sandbox` / `fs_deny_write`) |
| `Env` | Stable | Read every environment variable in the process snapshot (including credentials stored in env vars) and CLI arguments (`getArgs`), unless restricted via `--allow-env` / `--env-snapshot` |
| `Clock` | Stable | Monotonic/wall-clock timestamps (`now`) and `sleep` (supports deterministic virtual time with `--virtual-time`) |
| `Rand` | Stable | Random number generation (`randInt`, `randFloat`, `randBool`, `randSeed`; accepted by `--caps` and auto-grant, though omitted from `run --help`'s short `--caps` summary) |
| `Net` | Experimental | Outbound HTTP/HTTPS via `std/net` and `std/web`. Enforces HTTPS-only and blocks localhost, private IPs, and cloud metadata (`169.254.169.254`) by default unless widened with `--net-allow-http`, `--net-allow-localhost`, `--net-allow-metadata`, or `--net-allow-domains`; 30s timeout and 5 MB body cap by default |
| `Process` | Experimental | Spawns host commands (`std/process`). **Treat as full host access**: `Process` is not confined by `AILANG_FS_SANDBOX` alone (use `--process-allowlist` or `--policy` restricted mode) |
| `AI` | Experimental | Invokes configured LLM providers (`std/ai`), spending provider quota/credits (supports `--ai-stub` for offline testing) |
| `Stream` | Experimental | Opens bidirectional WebSocket and SSE connections (`std/stream`; WSS-only and private-IP blocking by default, 1 MB message cap) |
| `Secret` | Experimental | Resolves gated secrets (`std/secret`, e.g. `op://...`) into IFC-tainted values |
| `Trace` | Experimental | Emits OpenTelemetry-compatible custom spans and events (`std/trace`) |
| `SharedMem` | Experimental | Reads and writes shared key-value memory (`std/sharedmem`, `std/sem`) |
| `SharedIndex` | Experimental | Queries and upserts similarity-search indexes (`std/sharedindex`) |
| `DOM` | Experimental | Emits replayable DOM patches in browser/Cognitive-OS hosts (`std/dom`) |
| `Msg` | Experimental | Sends and receives Lamport-clocked fabric messages (`std/cognition`) |
| `Cog` | Experimental | Accesses Cognitive-OS event-log sinks (`std/cognition`) |

*(Note: `Debug` is a compile-time ghost effect with no runtime capability flag; `--release` erases it. `Declassify` is a compile-time IFC authority checked in effect rows and package `[effects].max` ceilings.)*

---

## Granting Authority (`--caps`, `--caps auto`, and `[bin]` Shims)

- **Explicit grant (`--caps IO,FS`):** Only listed capabilities are granted; calling any ungranted effect fails at runtime.
- **`--caps auto` and `[bin]` shims:** Passing `--caps auto` grants **every capability declared in the entrypoint's signature**. Installed package `[bin]` shims (`ailang pkg install`) default to `caps = "auto"` when `[bin].caps` is omitted in `ailang.toml`.
- **Rule for untrusted code:** Always inspect a module or package before running it with `--caps auto` or installing its `[bin]` shims — use `ailang inspect <file>`, `ailang iface <module>`, or `ailang pkg info <pkg>` to review declared effects and `[effects].max` ceilings.

---

## Confinement with `--policy` (Experimental)

For untrusted or agent-submitted programs, run with an operator-owned TOML policy file:

```bash
ailang run --policy /etc/ailang/agent-policy.toml untrusted.ail
```

- **Supervised execution:** The parent process resolves the policy, starts a child worker in its own process group, enforces `timeout_ms`, byte/output caps (`max_source_bytes`, `max_output_bytes`, `max_fs_transfer_bytes`), `allowed_caps`, `fs_sandbox`, `fs_deny_write` (read-only protected globs such as `.github/**`, `.git/**`), `net_allow`, and `[budgets]`.
- **Fail-closed flag refusal:** Widening CLI flags (`--caps`, `--entry`, `--env*`, `--net-*`, `--stream-*`, `--stdlib-path`, `--ai*`, `--fs-max-bytes`, etc.) are refused by name when `--policy` is set.
- **Modes:** `security_mode = "restricted"` (default) permits only effects with confined adapters; `trusted_host` is an explicit operator opt-in for host integrations with no confinement claim.
- See the [Agent Tool Policy guide](/docs/guides/agent-tool-policy) for the full policy schema.

### Package & Registry Confinement

When `AILANG_AGENT_POLICY` is set, all `ailang pkg` commands and the module loader refuse registry network fetches, `git clone`/`fetch`, and writes under `~/.ailang`. Operators can provision a read-only `AILANG_PACKAGE_ROOT` (`<vendor>/<name>/<version>`). Registry and git dependencies are verified against `ailang.lock`'s `content_hash` before compilation (content verification checks integrity against the lockfile, so protect the lockfile and package root from untrusted writes). See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/blob/dev/SECURITY.md#registry-and-package-confinement).

---

## Information-Flow Control (IFC) Labels (Experimental)

IFC labels (`T<label>`, sink refinements `T{not LABEL}`, and `! {Declassify}`) track explicit data flow in the type system at zero runtime cost and cross module boundaries (`#1134`).

**What IFC does NOT cover:**
- **Explicit flows only:** Labels do not track *implicit* control-flow channels (branching on a secret value to choose an unlabelled constant).
- **No runtime / storage persistence:** Labels erase at compile time and do not survive `FS`, `Net`, or `IO` round-trips.
- **Export annotation boundary:** Within one module, sink constraints are inferred for unannotated helper parameters (`#1719`); across module boundaries, an importer sees only what the exported signature explicitly annotates.

See the [IFC Labels guide](/docs/guides/ifc-labels) for examples and rules.

---

## Contracts & Z3 Static Verification

Functions may carry `requires { ... }` and `ensures { ... }` clauses checked statically by Z3 (`ailang verify` / `ailang check --verify`) or dynamically on the evaluator (`ailang run --verify-contracts`).

- **Bounded & model-scoped proofs:** Recursive functions and `map`/`filter`/`foldl` lambdas are unrolled to bounded depth unless bounded by `requires`; `int` is encoded as unbounded SMT `Int` (potential 64-bit runtime wraps surface as `int_overflow` caveats, or violations under `--int-model=int64`), and `float` inputs are assumed non-NaN.
- **Precondition trust:** `requires` is assumed when proving a function's own `ensures` and checked at calls made by *verified* callers; unverified callers and ordinary `ailang run` without `--verify-contracts` do not check `requires`.
- **Bytecode VM restriction:** `--verify-contracts` is evaluator-only and is refused alongside `--bytecode` / `--strict-bytecode` (`CTR004`, exit 2).
- **Exit codes:** `0` for `verified`, `no_obligations`, or `partial` (unless `--strict`); `1` for `unproved`, `inconclusive` (unless `--allow-inconclusive`), `counterexample`, `error`, or missing Z3 (`unavailable`); `2` for usage errors. See [Contracts & Verification](/docs/guides/contracts#exit-codes).

---

## Determinism Is Not Isolation

Program determinism — byte-identical outputs across the evaluator and bytecode VM for pure code and virtualized `Clock`/`Rand` — enables replay and auditability, **not** host isolation. A deterministic program granted `FS`, `Net`, `Env`, or `Process` still reads or modifies external host state unless confined by `--policy`, `AILANG_FS_SANDBOX`, or an OS sandbox.

---

## Supply Chain & Provenance

- **Release artifacts:** GitHub Releases (`v0.14.1`+) are keyless-signed with **Sigstore cosign** (`.sig` + `.pem` logged in Rekor) and carry **SLSA Build Level 3 provenance** (`multiple.intoto.jsonl`, `v0.15.x`+) alongside `SHA256SUMS`. See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/blob/dev/SECURITY.md#verifying-release-artifacts) for verification commands.
- **Dependencies:** `ailang.lock` (`ailang.lock/v1`) pins exact versions, `content_hash`, `interface_hash`, and declared effects, checked before compilation (`ailang lock --check`). Note that published registry packages are hash-verified via `ailang.lock`, **not** yet publisher-signed.

---

## Reporting Vulnerabilities

Please do **not** open public GitHub issues for security vulnerabilities. Report privately via **GitHub Security Advisories**:

- [https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/security/advisories/new](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/security/advisories/new)

See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/blob/dev/SECURITY.md) for response SLAs and scope.

---


# Reference: Stability

---
sidebar_position: 4
title: Stability Promise (1.x)
description: What syntax, stdlib, CLI, package format and hosted MCP tool surface AILANG guarantees across the 1.x release line.
reviewed: 2026-11-26
reviewBy: 2027-05-26
---

# AILANG 1.x Stability Promise

> **Ratified 2026-11-09.** Tier semantics follow [M-V1-STABILITY-PROMISE](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/blob/dev/design_docs/implemented/v0_29_0/m-v1-stability-promise.md), verified against `cmd/ailang`, `.stdlib-golden/`, `internal/pkg`, and the hosted MCP tool surface. Rows marked **⚠ close call** explain judgment calls.

## Tiers

| Tier | Promise | Marked in docs |
|------|---------|----------------|
| **Stable** | Covered by the 1.x promise; breaking changes require a **major** bump (`2.0`). Deprecations last at least one minor. | Default (listed below) |
| **Experimental** | Shipped and usable; **may change in a 1.x minor** with a CHANGELOG migration note. | `Experimental` banner / table |
| **Internal** | **No promise.** May change or be removed at any time. | `Internal` banner / table |

Additive changes (new modules, functions, optional flags, manifest keys, or MCP tools) may land in any minor. Items are drafted **Stable** when documented, exercised by `examples/`/evals/packages, and free of P0 defects.

## At a glance

| Area | Stable | Experimental | Internal | Source of truth |
|------|-------:|-------------:|---------:|-----------------|
| Stdlib modules | 17 | 31 | 3 | `std/STABILITY.toml` (module tiers) + `@experimental` (25 functions) → `.stdlib-golden/` |
| CLI commands | 19 | 23 | 46 | `cmd/ailang` dispatch table → [CLI Reference](/docs/reference/cli) |
| Package surface | 12 | 9 | 1 | `internal/pkg` manifest + lockfile code |
| Hosted MCP tools | 24 | 5 | 0 | `mcp_tools/`, `executor_tools/`, `executor_oauth/`, built-in `submit_feedback` |

## Syntax surface

Canonical syntax is defined by `ailang prompt` (`ailang prompt --version-active`) and [Language Syntax](/docs/reference/language-syntax).

- **Stable:** modules and imports (incl. `pkg/vendor/name/...`), `func`/`pure func` (`! {}`)/`export`, `let` and `{ …; … }`, lambdas (`\x. …`), `if … then … else …`, brace-form `match` with guards, ADTs, row-polymorphic records, `! {IO, FS, …}`, `::`/`++`, `"${expr}"` interpolation, `requires`/`ensures` contracts, and Stable effect capabilities (`IO`, `FS`, `Env`, `Clock`, `Rand`).
- **Error & option propagation (`let x = expr?`):** Unwraps `Ok`/`Some` on the return spine of a `Result`/`Option` function (`PAR_TRY_LET_ONLY` outside `let` on the spine).
- **Experimental syntax:** parameterised effects (`Net[scope=public]`, `@limit=N` — [Parameterised effects](/docs/guides/parameterised-effects)), IFC labels and `Declassify`, `serve-api` export annotations (`@route`, `@mcp_*`, `@noexpose`, `@nomcp`), and Experimental capabilities.
- **Retired / not implemented:** `match … with | …` emits `PAR019`; typed quasiquotes are not implemented ([Known Limitations](/docs/reference/limitations)).

## Stdlib surface

`make freeze-stdlib` writes `.stdlib-golden/` for top-level `std/*.ail` modules (`make verify-stdlib` checks `49` stdlib interfaces); `std/ai/streaming` and `std/stream/bridge` are subdirectory Experimental modules.

- **Stable contract:** export names, types, class constraints (`"constraints"`), literal-carrying numeric variables (`"literals"`), and effect rows.
- **Tier metadata:** module tiers live in [`std/STABILITY.toml`](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/blob/dev/std/STABILITY.toml) and per-function `@experimental` annotations surface in `ailang iface` and `ailang docs`.
- **`show` guarantee:** `show` is total, deterministic across evaluator and VM, and injective per type without NaN or functions (top-level strings unquoted; nested strings escaped; functions print `<function>`). `std/string.showPreview` is Stable with `std/string` (`…(+N chars)`).

### Stable stdlib (17)

| Module | Purpose | Evidence |
|--------|---------|----------|
| `std/io` | Console input/output | 221 example files, 28 benchmarks; the core effect surface |
| `std/list` | Linked-list operations | 126 examples, 21 benchmarks |
| `std/string` | String manipulation | 106 examples, 20 benchmarks |
| `std/result` | Error handling (`Ok`/`Err`) | 65 examples |
| `std/option` | Optional values (`Some`/`None`) | 57 examples |
| `std/json` | JSON encoding and decoding | 34 examples |
| `std/bytes` | Byte-slice operations | 29 examples |
| `std/fs` | Sandboxed file system | 20 examples; capability-gated |
| `std/env` | Environment variables (secure snapshot) | 12 examples |
| `std/array` | Fixed-size arrays with O(1) access | 11 examples, 4 benchmarks |
| `std/math` | Mathematical functions | 8 examples |
| `std/map` | Maps with deterministic key order | 7 examples |
| `std/clock` | Time operations (deterministic virtual time) | 6 examples |
| `std/rand` | Random number generation | 5 examples |
| `std/iter` | Iteration control primitives | 4 examples |
| `std/datetime` | Pure date and time operations | 4 examples |
| `std/set` | Immutable sets with deterministic order | ⚠ close call — newer (3 examples, 1 benchmark), but its surface mirrors `std/map` |

### Experimental stdlib (31)

| Module | Purpose | Why Experimental |
|--------|---------|------------------|
| `std/ai` | AI as a typed effect (`call`, `callJson`, `step`) | surface still changing along with the agent loop (20 examples) |
| `std/ai/streaming` | Token streaming for configured AI providers | subdirectory module, outside the freeze gate; narrow usage |
| `std/net` | HTTP client, plus pure `parseUrl` / `parseQuery` | ⚠ close call — widely used (17 examples), but security- and format-sensitive; the `Url` record shape may change |
| `std/web` | Web search and page fetch through a fixed backend | new; depends on one vendor's backend endpoint |
| `std/stream` | Async stream sources / `selectEvents` | close to concurrency; still changing |
| `std/stream/bridge` | WebSocket frame relay with an AILANG step | subdirectory module, outside the freeze gate; one example |
| `std/secret` | Gated secret resolution | newer effect |
| `std/process` | External command execution | ⚠ close call — host-boundary surface, tiered conservatively; the hosted executor is built on it |
| `std/crypto` | Cryptographic operations | ⚠ close call — security-sensitive, tiered conservatively |
| `std/jwt` | JWT parsing and verification | ⚠ close call — security-sensitive |
| `std/regex` | Linear-time (RE2) regex | RE2 subset; the `RegexMatch` record shape may change |
| `std/xml` | XML parsing and querying | ⚠ close call — the format surface may change |
| `std/yaml` | YAML to the `std/json` `Json` ADT | format surface; first-document-only semantics may widen |
| `std/html` | HTML5 parsing | the format surface may change |
| `std/zip` | ZIP archive read, write and stream | ⚠ close call — the format surface may change |
| `std/tar` | tar archive read and extract | the format surface may change |
| `std/gzip` | gzip compression | the format surface may change |
| `std/deflate` | Raw deflate (RFC 1951) and zlib (RFC 1950) | low-level and niche |
| `std/audio` | WAV/PCM boundaries and Ogg Opus encoding | new; niche |
| `std/terminal` | Native terminal host operations | new; host-specific scopes |
| `std/package` | Resolve files bundled in an installed package | the package-asset surface is still changing |
| `std/extension` | Helpers for AILANG extension packages | marked Experimental in its design doc |
| `std/cognition` | Cognitive-OS message fabric | marked Experimental in its design doc |
| `std/dom` | Cognitive-OS DOM substrate | marked Experimental in its design doc |
| `std/game` | Game-development utilities | marked Experimental in its design doc |
| `std/sem` | Semantic-caching types | marked Experimental in its design doc |
| `std/sharedmem` | Shared memory | marked Experimental in its design doc |
| `std/sharedindex` | Similarity-based semantic index | marked Experimental in its design doc |
| `std/embedding` | Vector-embedding utilities | niche |
| `std/simhash` | Locality-sensitive hashing | niche |
| `std/debug` | `Debug` ghost-effect logging | ⚠ close call — was Internal; moved because published packages (`sunholo/logging`) and the hosted executor depend on it |

### Experimental functions in Stable modules (25)

| Module | Functions | Why Experimental |
|--------|-----------|------------------|
| `std/json` | `repair`, `asBoolLoose`, `getStringArrayStrict`, `getNumberArrayStrict`, `decodeFloatArray` | boundary and niche helpers; no downstream use |
| `std/string` | `decodeQuotedPrintable`, `foldSlices`, `mapSlicesJoin`, `startsWithIgnoreCase` | niche; `foldSlices`/`mapSlicesJoin` take the function last, unlike every other higher-order export, and may be reordered |
| `std/list` | `takeMap`, `takeFlatMap` | workarounds for strict evaluation; redundant if fusion lands |
| `std/array` | `dot`, `axpy`, `scale`, `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `sum`, `argmax`, `scatterAdd`, `accumulate`, `encodeF64LE`, `decodeF64LE`, `encodeF32LE`, `decodeF32LE` | the numerics kernels, still growing; `axpy`/`scale` keep BLAS argument order |

### Deprecated stdlib names

Sixteen legacy 0.6x aliases were **removed in `v0.64.0`**; importing any removed alias fails with `IMP010` naming its replacement (run `sed -E -f tools/migrate-stdlib-renames.sed` for the 12 mechanical renames, and update `glob`, `slice`, `member`, `unsafeGet` by hand).

| Module | Deprecated | Use instead |
|--------|------------|-------------|
| `std/list` | `head_or`, `last_or`, `nth_or` | `headOr`, `lastOr`, `nthOr` |
| `std/list` | `member(x, xs)` | `contains(xs, x)` — the arguments swap |
| `std/string` | `charAt_or` | `charAtOr` |
| `std/math` | `abs_Int`, `abs_Float` | `absInt`, `absFloat` |
| `std/rand` | `rand_int`, `rand_float`, `rand_bool`, `rand_seed` | `randInt`, `randFloat`, `randBool`, `randSeed` |
| `std/fs` | `readFileBytes` | `readFileBase64` (it returns base64 text; `readFileRaw` returns bytes) |
| `std/fs` | `glob` | `walkWithSuffix` (a suffix filter, not a glob; the name stays retired for 1.x) |
| `std/io` | `printErr` | `eprint` (no newline; `eprintln` adds one) |
| `std/bytes` | `slice(b, start, len)` | `sliceLen` (the third argument is a length; the name stays retired for 1.x) |
| `std/array` | `unsafeGet` | `get` (identical behaviour) |

User packages may still apply Experimental `@deprecated("replacement")` (`TC_DEPRECATED_001`) and `@experimental` annotations to their own exports.

### Conventions of the Stable stdlib

- **Naming:** lowerCamelCase (exceptions: `PI()`, `E()`, `Json` builders `jn`/`jb`/`jnum`/`jint`/`js`/`ja`/`jo`/`kv`, and `intToStr`/`floatToStr` vs `stringToInt`/`stringToFloat`).
- **Argument order:** data first (`nth(xs, i)`, `map.lookup(m, k)`), except HOFs take function first (`map(f, xs)`, `foldl(f, acc, xs)`) and `list.take`/`list.drop`/`string.join`.
- **`Json` numbers:** `decode` produces `JInt(n)` for int64 literals and `JNumber(x)` otherwise; read numbers via `asNumber`/`getNumber`/`getInt`.

### Internal stdlib (3)

| Module | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `std/trace` | Custom trace span and event emission (telemetry-facing) |
| `std/trace_test` | Assertions over trace spans in tests |
| `std/smoke` | Helpers for package `_smoke.ail` boot probes |

## CLI surface

Command tiers match `cmd/ailang/commands.go` and [CLI Reference](/docs/reference/cli) (`make check-cli-docs`). Grouped top-level aliases and compatibility spellings (`ailang install` → `ailang pkg install`) inherit their canonical command's tier.

### Stable CLI (19)

| Command | Listed in | Also accepted | What it does |
|---------|-----------|---------------|--------------|
| `check` | top | `ai-check` | Type-check a file or directory; `--verify` adds contract verification |
| `docs` | top | — | Stdlib module documentation |
| `help` | top | — | Help for ailang, a group or a command |
| `init` | top | — | Scaffold a package (`init package`) or web app. ⚠ close call — it writes the Stable manifest; the web-app template may change |
| `prompt` | top | — | Emit the canonical teaching prompt |
| `repl` | top | — | Interactive REPL |
| `run` | top | — | Run a program (`--caps`, `--entry`, `--args-json`, `--args-file`) |
| `test` | top | — | Run tests (`--package`, `--json`) |
| `version` | top | — | Version, commit and build time |
| `pkg add` | pkg | `add` | Add a path, git or registry dependency |
| `pkg install` | pkg | `install` | Install a package (exact version or latest) and shim its `[bin]` commands |
| `pkg lock` | pkg | `lock` | Resolve dependencies and write `ailang.lock` (`--check` for read-only drift detection) |
| `pkg tree` | pkg | `tree` | Show the dependency tree |
| `pkg search` | pkg | `search` | Search the registry by keyword or tag |
| `pkg info` | pkg | — | Package detail: exports, effects, versions |
| `pkg versions` | pkg | — | Every version with its hashes |
| `pkg docs` | pkg | `pkg-docs` | Show a package's `AGENT.md` |
| `pkg publish` | pkg | `publish` | Publish the current package. ⚠ close call — the command and its manifest inputs are Stable, but the validator's `PUBnnn` gate set may tighten in a minor |
| `pkg bin` | pkg | `bin` | List or uninstall `[bin]` command shims. ⚠ close call — added in v0.40.0 |

- **Experimental flags on Stable commands:** `run --bytecode`, `run --policy`, `--ai*` / `--routing-*` / `--allow-routing`, `--budget-report`, resource caps (`--max-memory`, `--net-*`, `--fs-max-bytes`, `--process-allowlist`), `check --format agent`, and `ai-check` JSON report schema (`--no-verify`).
- **Stable contract behaviour:** `check --verify` exit codes follow [Contracts Guide](/docs/guides/contracts#exit-codes); `ailang run` checks contracts only with `--verify-contracts` (evaluator only; refused with `CTR004` on `--bytecode`).

## Packages

The 1.x promise covers manifest and lockfile **format and resolution semantics** ([Packages Guide](/docs/guides/packages), [Publishing Guide](/docs/guides/package-publishing)); individual packages declare their own maturity in `[stability].level`.

### Stable package surface (12)

| Surface | What is promised |
|---------|------------------|
| Manifest `[package]` | `name` (`vendor/name`), `version` (semver), `edition` (`"1"`), optional `ailang` min version, `module_prefix`, `description`, `license` |
| Manifest `[exports].modules` | Only listed modules are public; all others are package-private |
| Manifest `[dependencies]` | Exact pins only: `{ path = … }`, `{ git = …, tag/rev, subdir }`, or `"x.y.z"` (priority: path > git > registry) |
| Flat resolution | One version per package name; conflicts fail `ailang lock` explicitly |
| **Authority: effect ceiling** `[effects].max` | Compilation fails if package code declares or references an effect outside `max` (`max = []` = pure) |
| **Authority: ghost effects** | `Debug` is exempt from `[effects].max` and erased by `--release` |
| **Authority: run-time grant** | Capabilities come only from `run --caps` or `[bin].caps` (`auto` = entry's declared effects) |
| Manifest `[stability].level` | `experimental` / `stable` / `frozen` package-declared maturity |
| Lockfile `ailang.lock` | `schema: "ailang.lock/v1"` JSON recording hashes, effects, exports, and portable relative locators; `ailang lock --check` verifies drift |
| Dual hash model | `content_hash` tracks source bytes; `interface_hash` tracks exports/effects to prevent internal-refactor cascades |
| Import form | `import pkg/vendor/name/module (…)` resolves strictly via `ailang.lock` |
| Registry resolution | Default `https://storage.googleapis.com/ailang-registry` (`AILANG_REGISTRY` overrides); published versions are immutable |

### Experimental package surface (9)

| Surface | Why Experimental |
|---------|------------------|
| `[bin]` commands (`module`, `entry`, `caps`, `run_flags`) | ⚠ close call — used by `sunholo/email` / `eparse`; promote once shim layout settles |
| `[release].kind` and `CHANGELOG.md` `## <version>` | quality ladder still growing |
| Publish validator gates (`PUBnnn`, `ailang pkg quality`) | gates may tighten in a minor |
| Interface identity v2 hashing algorithm | ⚠ close call — hash meaning is Stable, algorithm may re-version |
| Confined-agent authority (`AILANG_AGENT_POLICY`, `AILANG_PACKAGE_ROOT`) | offline/sandbox policy still hardening |
| `[dependencies_dev]` | undocumented in package guide |
| `[ai_provider]`, `[extensions]`, `[assets]`, `[smoke]` | extension/provider wiring still changing |
| `[cascade]` and `pkg cascade` / `notify-upgrade` / `affected-by` | runs over Experimental message plane |
| `[metadata]` | free-form; no schema promised |

### Internal package surface (1)

| Surface | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| Registry administration (`pkg key`, `/rebuild-index`, `AILANG_REGISTRY_API_KEY`) | Operator-only |

### Worked example: `sunholo/mcp_oauth`

[`sunholo/mcp_oauth`](https://ailang.sunholo.com/docs/packages/sunholo/mcp_oauth) is consumed by `executor_oauth/` with exact pins, `[effects].max` covering referenced hook types (including `SharedMem`), and `ailang lock --check` verification:

```toml
# executor_oauth/ailang.toml (abridged)
[package]
name = "sunholo/ailang_executor_oauth"
module_prefix = "executor_oauth"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "1"
ailang = ">=0.54.0"

[exports]
modules = ["executor_oauth/oauth"]

[dependencies]
"sunholo/mcp_oauth" = "0.1.2"
"sunholo/firestore" = "0.7.2"
"sunholo/firebase_auth" = "0.1.2"

[effects]
max = ["IO", "FS", "Net", "Env", "Rand", "Clock", "Debug", "Declassify", "SharedMem"]
```

## Hosted MCP tool surface

Served by `serve-api` over `mcp_tools/`, `executor_tools/`, `executor_oauth/`, and built-in `submit_feedback` at `/mcp/` (IAM) and `/mcp/connect/` (OAuth 2.1, production host `https://executor.ailang.sunholo.com/mcp/connect/`).

For **Stable** tools, the promise covers tool name, input schema, hints, and response envelope (`{served_for, data}` / `{ok, exit_code, stdout, stderr, truncated}` / `ailang_check`'s `verification` field).

### Stable MCP tools (24)

| Tool | Source | What it does |
|------|--------|--------------|
| `ailang_prompt` | `executor_tools/` | The teaching prompt, in two parts (`part`: `core`, `reference`); `core` is meant to be called first |
| `ailang_check` | `executor_tools/` | Type-check source and verify contracts. ⚠ close call — the tool is Stable, but its `stdout` carries the `ai-check` JSON report, which is Experimental (see CLI) |
| `ailang_run` | `executor_tools/` | Run source in the sandbox. Only `IO` is granted, and the policy timeout applies |
| `ailang_eval` | `executor_tools/` | Evaluate one pure expression with `show()` |
| `ailang_builtins` | `executor_tools/` | Builtins with docs, filtered by `search` |
| `ailang_versions` | `mcp_tools/language.ail` | Versions the docs tools can serve |
| `prompt_get` | `mcp_tools/language.ail` | Teaching prompt for a version and kind |
| `stdlib_modules` | `mcp_tools/language.ail` | Stdlib module list |
| `stdlib_module` | `mcp_tools/language.ail` | One module's interface and docs |
| `stdlib_search` | `mcp_tools/language.ail` | Search stdlib functions |
| `limitations_list` | `mcp_tools/language.ail` | Known limitations |
| `effects_catalog` | `mcp_tools/language.ail` | Effect and capability catalog |
| `examples_list` | `mcp_tools/examples.ail` | Examples by feature and status |
| `example_get` | `mcp_tools/examples.ail` | One example's source |
| `example_for_concept` | `mcp_tools/examples.ail` | Best example for a concept |
| `docs_nav` | `mcp_tools/discovery.ail` | Docs navigation tree |
| `docs_search` | `mcp_tools/discovery.ail` | Search the docs |
| `changelog_for_version` | `mcp_tools/discovery.ail` | Changelog for a version |
| `install_guide` | `mcp_tools/install.ail` | Install steps for a harness and platform |
| `onboarding_guide` | `mcp_tools/onboarding.ail` | ⚠ close call — the `role` vocabulary may change |
| `design_docs_list` | `mcp_tools/design.ail` | ⚠ close call — exposes the repo's internal design-doc layout (`state`) |
| `design_doc` | `mcp_tools/design.ail` | ⚠ close call — as above |
| `roadmap` | `mcp_tools/design.ail` | ⚠ close call — as above |
| `executor_whoami` | `executor_oauth/oauth.ail` | ⚠ close call — the signed-in account, served only on `/mcp/connect/` at `executor.ailang.sunholo.com` |

### Experimental MCP tools (5)

| Tool | Source | Why Experimental |
|------|--------|------------------|
| `benchmarks_list` | `mcp_tools/benchmarks.ail` | ⚠ close call — eval data (eval tooling is Internal); the record shape follows the eval schema |
| `benchmarks_for_model` | `mcp_tools/benchmarks.ail` | ⚠ close call — as above |
| `benchmarks_compare` | `mcp_tools/benchmarks.ail` | ⚠ close call — as above |
| `submit_feedback` | built-in (`internal/apiserver/feedback_tool.go`) | ⚠ close call — the only write tool; rate-limited, and egress depends on deployment configuration |

## Support Window

| Release line | Bug fixes | Security fixes | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Latest `1.x` minor** | Yes | Yes | Upgrade to latest `1.x` minor (non-breaking by promise). |
| **Final `0.x` (`v0.64.x`)** | No | **90 days after `1.0.0`** | Critical/high security fixes only during the 90-day transition window. |
| **Older `1.x` / earlier `0.x`** | No | No | Upgrade to latest `1.x`. |

See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/blob/dev/SECURITY.md) for reporting channels and [Known Limitations](/docs/reference/limitations) / [Roadmap](/docs/roadmap) for current bounds and future work.

*Ratification status: **ratified 2026-11-09**.*

# Reference: CLI

---
sidebar_position: 13
title: CLI Reference
description: Every ailang command and group, generated from the dispatch table in cmd/ailang/commands.go — do not edit by hand.

# CLI Reference

Generated by `make docs-cli` from the dispatch table in `cmd/ailang/commands.go`.
Do not edit this page; edit the `Command` row and regenerate. `make check-cli-docs` fails
if the page and the table disagree.

## Finding a command

```bash
ailang --help              # the visible top level, one screen
ailang <group> --help      # everything filed in a group (dev, ops, eval)
ailang help <command>      # one command's own help
ailang <command> --help    # the same thing, spelled the other way
```

`--help` exits 0 at every level and runs nothing. An unknown command prints one line
and a suggestion on stderr and exits 1 — it does not dump the command list into your pipe.

## Output conventions

| Question | Flag | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Machine-readable output | `--json` | The one output-format flag. `ailang test --json`, not `--format json`. |
| Which model | `--model` | `ailang eval-suite --models` is accepted as an alias of the same target. |
| Where output goes | `--output` | Six of the seven sites. `ailang eval-publish --output-dir` is not converged yet. |
| Gate a mutation | `--dry-run` | Audited at all 14 sites: the default **acts**, and `--dry-run` is the opt-out everywhere. No command inverts it. |

Superseded spellings keep working — `ailang test --format json` still means `--json` —
because the fleet and fifteen frozen teaching prompts call them. They are not the spelling to
learn. Two commands keep a `--format` of their own for a reason that is not output format:
`ailang check --format agent` selects a third rendering (and `ailang ai-check` is
`ailang check --verify --format agent`), and `ailang exec --stream-json` is an NDJSON
event stream, which is not what `--json` means there.

Two commands parse `--format` by hand rather than registering it, so they do **not** accept
`--json` and were invisible to the flag audit that converged the rest:
`ailang eval-report --format=markdown|html|docusaurus|json|csv` and
`ailang doctor managed_agents --format=json`. Both need the `=` form. Converging them is a
follow-up, not a documentation problem.

## Contract verification flags

`ailang check --verify`, `ailang ai-check` and `ailang verify` share one exit rule
([contracts guide](/docs/guides/contracts#exit-codes)) and the flags that move it:

| Flag | On | Effect | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--strict` | all three (`check` only with `--verify`) | a skipped or inconclusive obligation fails | as the command (Stable on `check --verify`) |
| `--allow-inconclusive` | all three | an inconclusive result exits 0, even when it is the only obligation (nothing proved); `outcome` stays `inconclusive` | as the command (Stable on `check --verify`) |
| `--no-verify` | `ai-check` | type check only: the verifier does not run, `outcome` is `not_requested` (or `no_obligations`) | Experimental |

`--strict` with `--allow-inconclusive`, `--no-verify` with either, and `check --strict` without
`--verify` are usage errors (exit 2). Each command checks one file; a second file is a usage error.

## Groups are a drawer, not a rename

`ailang messages list` and `ailang ops messages list` are the same route. A group exists
so `ailang --help` fits on one screen; **every grouped command keeps its own top-level
spelling**, and no script, skill or launchd driver has to change.

## Commands

The visible top level: what `ailang --help` lists.

| Command | Also accepted | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ailang check` | `ailang ai-check` | Type-check a file or directory (--verify adds contract verification) |
| `ailang docs` | — | Show stdlib module documentation (--list to enumerate) |
| `ailang eval` | — | Benchmarks: run one, or a subcommand (suite, report, elo, ...) |
| `ailang examples` | — | Search and explore working code examples |
| `ailang fmt` | — | Format AILANG source (stdout / --write / --check) |
| `ailang help` | — | Show help for ailang, a group or a command |
| `ailang iface` | — | Print the normalized JSON interface of a module |
| `ailang init` | — | Scaffold a new AILANG package or web app |
| `ailang lsp` | — | Language Server Protocol server (for AI agents and IDEs) |
| `ailang pkg` | — | Package registry inspection and coordination |
| `ailang prompt` | — | Display the AILANG teaching prompt (for AI code generation) |
| `ailang repl` | — | Start the interactive REPL |
| `ailang run` | — | Run an AILANG program (--bytecode for the VM) |
| `ailang serve` | `ailang server` | Start the Observatory dashboard server (default port 1957) |
| `ailang test` | — | Run tests (--package for package mode) |
| `ailang verify` | — | Verify contracts and proof obligations |
| `ailang version` | — | Show version, commit hash and build time |

## `ailang dev` — Language-development and diagnostic commands

Reachable as `ailang dev <command>` and, unchanged, as `ailang <command>`.

| Command | Top-level spelling | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ailang dev agent-prompt` | `ailang agent-prompt` | Display the AILANG agent prompt |
| `ailang dev ast-edit` | `ailang ast-edit` | Structural edit of an AILANG declaration |
| `ailang dev axioms` | `ailang axioms` | Design axiom compliance scorecard |
| `ailang dev builtins` | `ailang builtins` | Inspect the builtin registry |
| `ailang dev cache` | `ailang cache`, `ailang brain` | Project brain / semantic cache operations |
| `ailang dev debug` | `ailang debug` | Debug AST and type information |
| `ailang dev devtools-prompt` | `ailang devtools-prompt` | Display the AILANG dev tools reference (for AI agents) |
| `ailang dev disasm` | `ailang disasm` | Disassemble compiled AILANG |
| `ailang dev doctor` | `ailang doctor` | Environment diagnostics (builtins, memory, managed_agents, ...) |
| `ailang dev editor` | `ailang editor` | Install editor syntax highlighting (vscode, vim, neovim) |
| `ailang dev export-training` | `ailang export-training` | Export traces as AI training data |
| `ailang dev generate-extension-registry` | `ailang generate-extension-registry` | Emit the static extension dispatch file from [extensions] |
| `ailang dev inspect` | `ailang inspect` | Semantic module X-ray (types, signatures, effects, contracts, calls) |
| `ailang dev micro-rag` | `ailang micro-rag`, `ailang microrag`, `ailang urag` | Micro-RAG index and retrieval operations |
| `ailang dev pi` | `ailang pi` | Manage pi extensions (install, uninstall, status) |
| `ailang dev policy-check` | `ailang policy-check` | Evaluate a policy program against its cases |
| `ailang dev policy-tool` | `ailang policy-tool` | Typed tool endpoint of the ailang_only lane: one JSON request on stdin, one response on stdout |
| `ailang dev replay` | `ailang replay` | Replay and verify against a recorded trace |
| `ailang dev sandbox-check` | `ailang sandbox-check` | Diagnose FS sandbox path resolution (AILANG_FS_SANDBOX) |
| `ailang dev select-best` | `ailang select-best` | Pick the best candidate from generated variants |
| `ailang dev watch` | `ailang watch` | Watch a file for changes and re-run it |

## Removed commands

Routes whose feature was removed. They are still accepted only so an old caller
gets a message naming the replacement (in the summary); every invocation but --help exits 1.

| Route | Use instead | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ailang compile` | — | Removed: the Go emitter; use `ailang run` (--bytecode for the VM) |

## Documentation search

`ailang docs search "query"` searches the local `design_docs/` or `docs/` corpus first, and
falls back to GitHub code search when run outside a source checkout. The fallback requires
authentication — `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `gh auth login`; unauthenticated search is not attempted.
`--path <dir>` forces a local corpus and `--no-github` (or `AILANG_NO_GITHUB_SEARCH`) disables the
fallback. GitHub results are cached per query for one hour under
`~/.ailang/cache/docsearch/github/`; a cache entry holds results and metadata only, never tokens.

When `AILANG_AGENT_POLICY` is set, the whole GitHub backend is operator authority.
It refuses before credential discovery, cache reads (including valid hits), HTTP or cache
writes, including when invoked through `policy-tool`. Provide local docs and use
`--path <dir>`, or ask the operator to run GitHub search outside the sandbox. Default
local SimHash search remains available; explicit neural/embedding and cache-management
modes have separate behavior and are not covered by this GitHub-only restriction.

## Startup contract

Language commands — the ones you run to work *with* AILANG rather than to operate the fleet —
open no observatory database and run no git probe at startup. This is a contract with a test
behind it (`cmd/ailang/commands_probe_test.go` counts the probes), not a presentation choice,
and it holds for a command's group spelling too: `ailang dev builtins` is as quiet as
`ailang builtins`.

The language commands are `ast-edit`, `builtins`, `check`, `debug`, `devtools-prompt`, `disasm`, `docs`, `examples`, `export-training`, `fmt`, `help`, `iface`, `init`, `inspect`, `lsp`, `prompt`, `repl`, `replay`, `run`, `select-best`, `test`, `verify`, `version`, `watch`.

# Reference: Reserved Keywords

---
title: Reserved Keywords
reviewed: 2026-11-26
reviewBy: 2027-05-26
---

# Reserved Keywords

The lexer keyword map contains **41 entries**. Most cannot be used as names.
The four contextual testing words remain legal identifiers where a testing marker
is not expected; their reservation is contextual, not global. `case` is an ordinary
identifier, not a keyword. No words are released by this diagnostic change.

A reserved word in a parameter name produces `PAR_RESERVED_KEYWORD` at that word.
The invalid parameter is dropped for parser recovery; the source still fails checking.
Record-type fields retain `PAR_FIELD_NAME_EXPECTED` with a reservation explanation.
Rename the parameter and all of its uses before checking again.

## Complete keyword map

| Word | Current use or reservation, owner and trigger |
| --- | --- |
| `func` | Function declaration or parenthesized function literal. |
| `pure` | Pure function marker. |
| `let` | Immutable binding. |
| `letrec` | Recursive binding. |
| `in` | Binding scope. |
| `if` | Conditional or match guard. |
| `then` | Conditional true branch. |
| `else` | Conditional false branch. |
| `match` | Pattern matching with braces (no `with`). |
| `with` | PAR019 dialect detection and planned effect-handler syntax. Handler lane: consume or release at syntax freeze. Alternatives: `using`, `given`, `w`. |
| `type` | Type declaration. |
| `class` | Type-class declaration syntax. |
| `instance` | Type-class instance syntax. |
| `module` | Module declaration. |
| `import` | Import declaration. |
| `export` | Export marker. |
| `extern` | Reserved. `extern func` still parses, but every declaration is `EXT004`: extern functions were implemented only by the removed Go emitter, and no engine runs them. Write the function in AILANG, or use a std function or an effect. |
| `forall` | Universal type quantification. |
| `exists` | Reserved for existential type quantification; the type-system lane must consume or release it at syntax freeze. |
| `test` | Contextual named test marker; also a legal identifier. |
| `tests` | Contextual test block marker; also a legal identifier. |
| `property` | Contextual property marker; also a legal identifier. |
| `properties` | Contextual property block marker; also a legal identifier. |
| `assert` | Reserved for planned assertion builtin; assertion/testing lane must consume or release at syntax freeze. Alternatives: `check`, `verify`. |
| `spawn` | Reserved for planned concurrency lane (CSP/session types). Consume or release at concurrency syntax freeze. Alternatives: `chan`, `fork`, `concurrent`, `pick`. |
| `parallel` | Reserved for planned concurrency lane (CSP/session types). Consume or release at concurrency syntax freeze. Alternatives: `chan`, `fork`, `concurrent`, `pick`. |
| `select` | Reserved for planned concurrency lane (CSP/session types). Consume or release at concurrency syntax freeze. Alternatives: `chan`, `fork`, `concurrent`, `pick`. |
| `channel` | Reserved for planned concurrency lane (CSP/session types). Consume or release at concurrency syntax freeze. Alternatives: `chan`, `fork`, `concurrent`, `pick`. |
| `send` | Reserved for planned CSP/session-types lane. CSP lane: consume or release at syntax freeze. Alternatives: `tx`, `rx`, `deadline`, `expires`. |
| `recv` | Reserved for planned CSP/session-types lane. CSP lane: consume or release at syntax freeze. Alternatives: `tx`, `rx`, `deadline`, `expires`. |
| `timeout` | Reserved for planned CSP/session-types lane. CSP lane: consume or release at syntax freeze. Alternatives: `tx`, `rx`, `deadline`, `expires`. |
| `as` | Import alias. |
| `deriving` | Type-class derivation. |
| `requires` | Precondition contract. |
| `ensures` | Postcondition contract. |
| `invariant` | Invariant contract. |
| `true` | Boolean literal. |
| `false` | Boolean literal. |
| `not` | Boolean negation. |
| `and` | Boolean conjunction. |
| `or` | Boolean disjunction. |

## Reservation decisions

The [effect-handler lane](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/blob/dev/design_docs/planned/v1_1_0/m-effect-handlers.md)
owns the proposed `handle ... with` syntax. Its syntax freeze must explicitly
consume `with` as syntax or release it. This is separate from its current PAR019
role: `match x with { ... }` is rejected with the existing dialect diagnostic;
AILANG uses `match x { ... }` and guards use `if`.

The [CSP/session-types lane](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/blob/dev/design_docs/planned/v1_1_0/m-csp-session-types.md)
owns channel communication and concurrency reservations. Its examples are
unfrozen sketches, including function-form receive/send; they do not establish
that those words need keyword status. At syntax freeze the lane must explicitly
consume or release each listed word. The assertion/testing lane has the same
obligation for its planned assertion builtin (see the
[named-test assertion plan](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/blob/dev/design_docs/implemented/v0_33_1/m-named-test-assert-lowering-sprint-plan.md)).
No syntax-freeze decision is made here. Until its owner rules, each reservation
remains. A release must update the keyword map, token enum, token strings,
`IsKeyword`, and this reference together.

## Working rename example

```ailang
module examples/runnable/reserved_keyword_names

pure func combine(a: int, rx: int, b: int) -> int = a + rx + b
pure func usingValue(using: int) -> int = using
export pure func main() -> int = combine(1, 2, 3) + usingValue(4)
```

Use `ailang check examples/runnable/reserved_keyword_names.ail` to check the
corrected three-parameter call. Recovery of an invalid parameter is not a
successful type check and does not preserve a three-argument call's arity.

See [Language Syntax](./language-syntax.md), or run `ailang prompt` for the
current teaching prompt and `ailang check file.ail` for diagnostics.

# Reference: Known Limitations

---
sidebar_position: 5
title: Known Limitations
description: Live-verified capability & cliff matrix, workarounds, and design constraints in AILANG
reviewed: 2026-11-26
reviewBy: 2027-05-26
---

# AILANG Known Limitations

**Live-verified at AILANG `v0.64.1` (`2026-11-26`).** Every entry below reflects measured compiler, verifier, or runtime behavior rather than historical speculation. See [Design Documents](/docs/design-docs) for implemented features and [Stability Promise](/docs/reference/stability) for tier guarantees.

## Capability & Cliff Matrix

| Area / Construct | Measured Behavior (`v0.64.1`) | Workaround / Guard |
|---|---|---|
| **`int` wrap vs `verify --int-model=int64`** | Runtime `int` wraps at signed 64-bit (`9223372036854775807 + 1 == -9223372036854775808`). `ailang verify` defaults to unbounded Z3 `Int` (emitting an `int_overflow` caveat note); `--int-model=int64` promotes overflow to `VIOLATION`. | Pass `ailang verify --int-model=int64` or bound inputs in `requires`. |
| **Non-tail recursion (~5 KB/frame) & depth cap** | `ailang run` caps recursion at `10,000` levels/frames by default (`RT_REC_003` on evaluator, `stack overflow` on VM). Non-tail recursion allocates ~5 KB/frame (evaluator hops goroutines every `131,072` levels). | Use tail recursion (constant depth) or `std/list` (`map`, `foldl`, `takeMap`), or pass `--max-recursion-depth N`. |
| **List prepend (`::`, `++`) & strict `take`** | `ListValue` is a flat Go slice, so `x :: xs` and `xs ++ [x]` copy `O(n)` per step (`O(n²)` in loops). Arguments are strict: `take(n, flatMap(f, xs))` materialises the whole `flatMap` first. | Use `map`, `takeMap`, `takeFlatMap`, or `foldl` with a scalar/record accumulator. |
| **Bounded Z3 recursion & verification scope** | `ailang verify` unrolls named recursion (`--verify-recursive-depth N`, default `2`) and literal-lambda HOFs (`map`/`filter`/`foldl`/`any`/`flatMap`, depth `3`). Unbounded recursion is `inconclusive` (no induction). Bitwise ops (`&`, `^`, `~`, `<<`, `>>`) and function parameters are `skipped`; floats model as SMT `Real` (non-NaN input assumed; `/0`, `sqrt(<0)`, `log(<=0)` are violations); opaque helpers note `helpers_not_checked`. | Bound depth/lengths in `requires`, guard floats with `std/math.isNaN`, and run runtime contract checks via `ailang run --verify-contracts` (evaluator only; `--bytecode --verify-contracts` errors `CTR004`). |
| **Explicit-flow IFC (`T<label>`, `Declassify`)** | Information-flow labels track **explicit data flow** only, not implicit control-flow channels (branching on a tainted boolean to return untainted literals). Parameters allow one `not` refinement (`string{not a, not b}` does not parse). | Use explicit `Declassify` at boundary functions; group forbidden labels under a shared parent label (`string{not sensitive}`). |
| **`--bytecode` VM coverage & parity** | `186 / 205` runnable examples run natively on the VM (`~40×` faster than the evaluator on call-heavy code). Remaining gaps (unwired effect builtins, contract-module ADTs, user ADTs/closures passed to evaluator-only helpers, newtype `w.x` access) warn on stderr (`BC001` under `--strict-bytecode`). `Map.insert`/`Set.insert`/`Array.set` copy `O(n)` per update; module-level `let` initializers recompute per read on VM. | Run `ailang check --strict-bytecode` in CI to catch fallbacks; build collections via `fromList`/`updateMany`/`accumulate`; cache expensive module `let` values in locals. |
| **`export import` re-export syntax** | `export import std/io (println)` fails with `PAR_EXPORT_REQUIRES_FUNC` (pending open PR `#2475`). | Define an `export func` wrapper in the facade module. |
| **No ad-hoc user typeclasses** | Built-in classes (`Num`, `Eq`, `Ord`, `Show`, `Fractional`) and `deriving (Eq, Json)` work; user `class`/`instance` definitions, explicit constraints (`Num a => ...`), and higher-kinded type params (`m[int]`, `PAR_TYPE_PARAM_APPLIED`) are unsupported. | Pass explicit record-of-functions dictionaries or use ADTs. |
| **Type size & WASM checker budgets** | `check` rejects types >`65,536` nodes / `1,000` depth (`TC_TYPE_SIZE_001`) or excessive alias expansion work (`TC_TYPE_WORK_001`). Browser WASM adds a `2 s` wall-clock type-check budget (`ailangSetTypeCheckBudget` adjusts; CLI unaffected). | Extract helper functions or nominal ADTs for huge record/match chains; flatten nested matches. |
| **Syntax & stdlib constraints** | Multi-statement `if`/`else` branches require `{ ... }`; `let x = expr?` works on `let` bindings along a `Result`/`Option` return spine (`PAR_TRY_LET_ONLY` elsewhere); no Y-combinator/infinite types (`TC004`); no typed quasiquotes or CSP channels; `std/regex` uses RE2 (no backreferences/lookaround); `std/json` integers outside int64 decode as `JNumber(float)`; `std/terminal` native keys are macOS/Linux only. | Wrap multi-statement `else` in `{ ... }`; use `"${expr}"` interpolation; keep >53-bit JSON IDs as strings. |
| **Policy confinement residuals (`--policy`)** | Confined execution covers mediated effects (`IO`, `FS`, `Net`, `Clock`, `Rand`, `Stream`). CPU/RAM limits require containers/cgroups; HTTP proxies (`E_NET_PROXY_REFUSED`) and loopback/metadata are refused in restricted mode; `std/ai` HTTP bypasses `Net` pinning (spend capped by `[budgets] AI`); Windows/WASM lack restricted process teardown. | Run untrusted workers in a container/cgroup (`AILANG_EVAL_MAX_RSS`), use `trusted_host` for local Ollama, and set `fs_deny_write` on supply-chain files. |

## Minimal Verified Workarounds

### 1. Int64 Overflow & Z3 Verification (`--int-model=int64`)

```ailang
module docs/limits_int64

export pure func incBounded(x: int) -> int
  requires { x >= 0 && x < 9223372036854775807 }
  ensures { result > x }
{
  x + 1
}
```

Without the upper bound in `requires`, `ailang verify --int-model=int64` flags `x = 9223372036854775807` as `VIOLATION (int_overflow)` instead of an advisory caveat.

### 2. Tail Recursion & Builtin-Backed Loops (`RT_REC_003`)

```ailang
module docs/limits_recursion

import std/list (foldl, takeMap)

export pure func sumAcc(n: int, acc: int) -> int =
  if n <= 0 then acc else sumAcc(n - 1, acc + n)

export pure func topDoubled(xs: [int], k: int) -> [int] =
  takeMap(k, \x. x * 2, xs)

export pure func sumList(xs: [int]) -> int =
  foldl(\acc x. acc + x, 0, xs)
```

`sumAcc` runs in constant stack depth on both engines; `takeMap` avoids allocating unvisited elements under strict evaluation.

### 3. Re-exporting Symbols (`export import` Pending `#2475`)

```ailang error=PAR_EXPORT_REQUIRES_FUNC
-- Fails today with PAR_EXPORT_REQUIRES_FUNC:
module docs/limits_reexport_fail
export import std/io (println)
```

Workaround — wrap the imported symbol in an exported function:

```ailang
module docs/limits_reexport_ok

import std/io (println)

export func logLine(msg: string) -> () ! {IO} = println(msg)
```

### 4. Named Recursion, Explicit Braces & RE2 Regex

```ailang
module docs/limits_syntax_regex

import std/regex (compile)

export pure func factorial(n: int) -> int =
  if n <= 1 then 1 else n * factorial(n - 1)

export pure func buildDoubles(x: int, maxX: int) -> [int] =
  if x > maxX then [] else {
    let v = x * 2;
    let rest = buildDoubles(x + 1, maxX);
    v :: rest
  }

export pure func checkRegex() -> bool =
  match compile("(a)\\1") {
    Ok(_) => true,
    Err(_) => false   -- RE2 rejects backreferences cleanly with Err
  }
```

### 5. Callback Effect Contracts & Type Bounds

- **Function-field annotations:** Storing an `! {IO, Env}` callback in a record typed `{f: int -> int ! {IO}}` still type-checks (closed upper-bound enforcement remains tracked in `#573`/`#1326`), though invoking annotated fields and `mapE` does charge effects. Use closed pure `T -> U ! {}` for pure callbacks (`std/list.map`).
- **Rigid signature variables & recursive groups:** Explicit `[a]` / implicit lowercase type variables are rigid (`TC_RIGID_001`). Calls inside a recursive group are monomorphic (no polymorphic recursion).
- **Named tests:** `test "..." { ... }` and `property "..." { ... }` bodies are checked pure (`TC_TEST_001`) and do not enforce callee contracts at runtime; verify effectful paths via an exported `main` with `ailang run --caps ... --verify-contracts`.

## Recently Resolved (Now Shipped)

- **Error/option spine propagation (`let x = expr?`):** Unwraps `Ok`/`Some` along a return spine and early-returns `Err`/`None` (see [Option vs Result](/docs/reference/option-vs-result)).
- **Two engines only (`Go` emitter removed):** `compile --emit-go` was removed after `v0.60.5`; AILANG runs exclusively on the reference evaluator and `--bytecode` VM.
- **Exhaustive pattern checks & nominal identity:** `TC_MATCH_002` checks pattern exhaustiveness, `TC_NOMINAL_001` enforces nominal ADT identity across modules, and `TC_CONSTRAINT_001` propagates class constraints across module boundaries.
- **Per-instance numeric compilation (`#2378`):** Generic numeric functions with integer literals (`func inc(x) = x + 1`) compile both `int` and `float` variants (up to 4 literal-carrying type vars; `TC_NUMVAR_001` otherwise).

## Reporting New Limitations

File an issue at [github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/issues](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/issues) with `ailang --version`, a minimal `.ail` reproduction, and expected vs actual behavior.

---


# AI Teaching Prompt (Latest: v0.16.20)

# AILANG v0.16.20 - AI Teaching Prompt (with IFC Labels + Output Discipline)

AILANG is a **pure functional language** with Hindley-Milner type inference and algebraic effects. Write code using **recursion** (no loops), **pattern matching**, and **explicit effect declarations**.

**⚠️ AILANG is NOT Python!** Do not use Python syntax like `def`, `for`, `while`, `class`, or `if x:`. See "What AILANG Does NOT Have" below.

## Required Program Structure

```ailang
module myproject/mymodule

export func main() -> () ! {IO} {
  println(show(42))  -- println is in prelude, no import needed!
}
```

**Rules:**
1. First line MUST be `module path/name` matching the file path
2. Use `println(show(value))` for numbers, `println(str)` for strings. **Prefer `show` over `intToStr`/`floatToStr`** — `show` works on ALL types
3. **Pick ONE function-body style per function and stick to it:**
   - **Block body** `func f() ! {IO} { ... }` — one `let` per line, NO `in`. Statements are separated by newlines (canonical, what `ailang fmt` writes) or by `;` (also accepted)
   - **Expression body** `func f() ! {IO} = let x = a in let y = b in finalExpr` — `in` keyword, NO semicolons
   - **The `= {` trap**: `func f() = { a; b }` mixes both styles. `=` means expression body (no `;`); for multiple statements DROP the `=` → `func f() { a; b }`. (Error: `PAR017: ';' is only valid inside { } block bodies`.)
4. No loops — use recursion
5. **Output raw AILANG code only** — no markdown fences (`` ``` ``), no prose, no JSON wrappers. The first line must be `module ...`.

## println vs print

| Function | Import Required? | Behavior |
|----------|-----------------|----------|
| `println` | NO (prelude) | WITH newline |
| `print` | YES (`import std/io (print)`) | NO newline |

```ailang
module examples/print_demo
import std/io (print)

export func main() -> () ! {IO} {
  -- println works without import in entry modules (prelude provides it)
  println("A")
  println("B")  -- Output: A\nB\n

  -- print requires import for no-newline output
  print("A")
  print("B")    -- Output: AB
}
```

**Use `println` for most output.** Use `print` ONLY when building output on one line.

**Real-time terminal output (games, progress bars, TUIs), v0.27.0+:** on a TTY, stdout is
line-buffered — `println` shows at once, but partial-line output (`\r` with no newline) needs
an explicit `flush()`. C-style escapes `\xHH` / `\u{..}` / `\e` / `\0` work in string literals.

```ailang
import std/io (print, flush)

func showProgress() -> () ! {IO} {
  print("\r\u{1B}[92m50%\u{1B}[0m")  -- \u{1B} (or \x1b) = ESC (ANSI colour); "\x1b[2J" clears the screen
  flush()                             -- force it to the screen NOW (no /dev/tty hack needed)
}
```
Runs under `--caps IO,Clock` — no `FS`. `eprint`/`eprintln` (std/io) write to stderr (unbuffered).

## Line input and native terminals (supporting runtime required)

Use `import std/io (readLineOpt)` for loops that must distinguish a blank line
from EOF: `readLineOpt() -> Option[string] ! {IO}` returns `Some("")` for a blank
line, `Some(text)` for a final unterminated line, then sticky `None` at EOF.
Legacy `readLine() -> string` returns `""` for both EOF and blank input; do not
use that equality to terminate a line service.

```ailang
module line_echo
import std/io (readLineOpt, println)
import std/option (Some, None)
func loop() -> () ! {IO} {
  match readLineOpt() {
    None => (),
    Some(line) => { println(line); loop() }
  }
}
export func main() -> () ! {IO} = loop()
```

Native immediate keys/resize use `std/terminal` under `IO`: `info()` queries
configured TTY endpoints, `withTerminal(options, body)` owns restoration, and
`readEvent(session, timeout_ms)` returns `Result[TerminalEvent, TerminalError]`.
Timeouts: `-1` blocks, `0` polls, `1..60000` waits in milliseconds. `Idle` is
separate from `EndOfInput`. Callback effects propagate as `{IO, e}`. Native
scopes require macOS/Linux and host signal lifecycle integration; other hosts
return `Unsupported`. Handle errors explicitly. Widgets and normalized replay
belong in `sunholo/terminal_ui`; no shell or `/dev/tty` workaround is required.

## Output Discipline (stdout is compared byte-for-byte)

Your program's printed output is graded by an **exact match** against the expected
result. Extra text — even when the computed value is correct — is a failure.

- **Print only what the task asks for, nothing more.** If the task wants `40`, print
  `40` — never `Result: 40`, `Answer: 40`, or `The result is 40`.
- **No labels, captions, or prefixes** in front of values. If the task says to print
  `a = TBool`, that exact string is the whole line — do not add `Types unify!` or any
  other commentary before or after it.
- **No status / confirmation lines** ("Done", "Success", "They unify!", "Computing…")
  unless the task explicitly tells you to print them.
- **Match the requested format exactly**: same capitalisation, same spacing, one value
  per line as specified, and no extra trailing or leading blank lines.
- When the task says *"print the result"* or *"print if they unify"*, it means print
  the bare value(s) it just defined — not a sentence describing them.

Treat the expected output as a contract: emit exactly those characters and stop.

## CLI Exploration (USE THIS!)

**Before writing helper functions, check if the stdlib already has what you need:**

```bash
ailang docs --list              # List all stdlib modules
ailang docs std/string          # Show ALL exports with signatures
ailang docs std/list            # Show list operations
ailang builtins list            # All registered builtins
ailang check file.ail           # Type-check without running (use _? or ?name holes to query expected type + locals)
ailang check --fix file.ail     # Auto-apply safe mechanical fixes (trailing ';', '=' before '{', TC_MATCH_002 stubs, missing ! {Effects}, string '++' -> "${...}"; also exposed via LSP codeAction)
ailang inspect <file-or-dir>    # <100ms 1-line/symbol semantic X-ray: types, deriving, exports+locals, ! {Effects}, contracts, callees (--json, --exports-only)
ailang examples search "recursion"  # Find working code examples
```

## Quick Reference Examples

**Print calculation:**
```ailang
module benchmark/solution
import std/io (println)
export func main() -> () ! {IO} = println(show(5 % 3))
```

**If-then-else** (always use `then`/`else`, not C-style `if x { ... }`; unbraced multi-statement `let` branches are accepted and `ailang fmt` normalizes them to `{ ... }`):
```ailang
module benchmark/solution
import std/io (println)
export func main() -> () ! {IO} {
  let x = 10;
  let msg = if x > 0 then "positive" else "not positive";
  println(msg)
}
```

**HTTP GET:**
```ailang
module benchmark/solution
import std/net (httpGet)
export func main() -> () ! {IO, Net} = println(httpGet("https://example.com"))
```

**HTTP POST with JSON:**
```ailang
module benchmark/solution
import std/net (httpPost)
import std/json (encode, jo, kv, js, jnum)
export func main() -> () ! {IO, Net} {
  let data = encode(jo([kv("message", js("hello")), kv("count", jnum(42.0))]));
  println(httpPost("https://httpbin.org/post", data))
}
```

**Filter list recursively:**
```ailang
module benchmark/solution
export func filter(people: [{name: string, age: int}], minAge: int) -> [{name: string, age: int}] =
  match people {
    [] => [],
    p :: rest => if p.age >= minAge then p :: filter(rest, minAge) else filter(rest, minAge)
  }
```

**Record update (immutable):**
```ailang
module benchmark/solution
export func main() -> () ! {IO} {
  let person = {name: "Alice", age: 30, city: "NYC"};
  let older = {person | age: person.age + 1};         -- Update one field
  let moved = {older | city: "SF"};                   -- Chain updates
  println("${person.name}, ${show(person.age)}, ${person.city}");
  println("${older.name}, ${show(older.age)}, ${older.city}");
  println("${moved.name}, ${show(moved.age)}, ${moved.city}")
}
```

**Open records (width subtyping):**
```ailang
module benchmark/solution

-- EXACT record: only accepts {name: string}, rejects extra fields
pure func getNameExact(p: {name: string}) -> string = p.name

-- OPEN record with | r: accepts extra fields
pure func getName(p: {name: string | r}) -> string = p.name

-- OPEN record with ... sugar (equivalent to | r with fresh variable)
pure func getEmail(u: {email: string, ...}) -> string = u.email

export func main() -> () ! {IO} {
  -- Exact: only works with exact shape
  println(getNameExact({name: "Alice"}));

  -- Open: accepts any record with at least name field
  println(getName({name: "Bob", age: 30}));
  println(getName({name: "Charlie", age: 25, city: "NYC"}));

  -- Ellipsis sugar: same behavior
  println(getEmail({email: "test@example.com", name: "Test", id: 123}))
}
```

**AI effect (call LLM):**
```ailang
module benchmark/solution
import std/ai (call, callJson, callJsonSimple)
export func main() -> () ! {IO, AI} = println(call("What is 2+2?"))
```

## What AILANG Does NOT Have

| Invalid | Use Instead |
|-----------|----------------|
| `for`/`while` loops | Recursion |
| `[x*2 for x in xs]` | `map(\x. x*2, xs)` or recursion |
| `range(n)` | `range(0, n)`: two args, end exclusive |
| `acc ++ [x]` / `A.set` / `M.insert` once per loop step | O(n²): build in one pass, see "Cost Model" |
| `var`/`let mut` | Immutable `let` bindings |
| `list.map()` | `map(f, list)` |
| `import "std/io"` | `import std/io (println)` |
| `{"key": "val"}` | `jo([kv("key", js("val"))])` |
| `f(a)(b)` for multi-arg func | `f(a, b)` - multi-arg funcs use commas |
| `if x { ... }` | `if x then ... else ...` (wrap multi-statement `then`/`else` bodies in `{ ... }`: `if x then { let a = 1; a } else 0`) |
| `func f[a: Ord](...)` | `func f[a](...)` — typeclass constraints (`Eq`, `Ord`, `Num`) are inferred automatically |
| mixing `let x = e in` with `;` | Use ONE style consistently |
| `let Some(x) = opt` (refutable `let`) | Use `match opt { Some(x) => ..., None => ... }` (irrefutable `let (a, b) = pair` and `let { name, age } = r` / `let { port: p, ... } = cfg` ARE supported) |
| `\a, b. body` (unparenthesized commas) | Multi-arg: `\a b. body` (space-separated, called `f(a, b)`). Tuple param destructuring: `\(a, b). body`. Record param destructuring: `\{ x, y }. body`. Named: `func(a: T, b: U) -> R { body }` |
| nested `func f(...) =` | Use `let f = \x. body` for nested functions |
| `!condition` | Both `!x` and `not x` work — prefer `not` for readability |
| `concat(a, b)` for strings | `"${a}${b}"` interpolation — `++` is list-only in v0.13.0+ |
| `concat(a, b)` for lists | `a ++ b` |

## Let Bindings: Block Style vs Expression Style

**Rule: Inside `{ }` blocks, one `let` per line (no `in`). With `=` bodies, use `in`.**

```ailang
import std/io (println)

-- Block style: curly braces, one statement per line (canonical `ailang fmt` form)
func blockStyle() -> () ! {IO} {
  let x = 1
  let y = 2
  println(show(x + y))
}

-- `;` between block statements is also accepted (fmt removes it)
func semicolonStyle() -> () ! {IO} {
  let x = 1;
  let y = 2;
  println(show(x + y))
}

-- Block-ending record updates, tuples, and lists work directly on a new line (no `;` needed)
pure func bump(r: {a: int}) -> {a: int} {
  let x = 1
  {r | a: x}
}

-- Tuple destructuring in let (block style or `in` style; nested tuples and `_` supported)
pure func swap(p: (int, string)) -> (string, int) {
  let (n, s) = p
  (s, n)
}

-- Expression style: equals + in
func exprStyle() -> () ! {IO} =
  let x = 1 in
  let y = 2 in
  println(show(x + y))
```

```not-ailang
-- WRONG: Using `in` inside `{ }` block causes scope errors
export func main() -> () ! {IO} {
  let x = 1 in   -- DON'T use `in` inside blocks!
  let y = 2;     -- ERROR: x out of scope
  println(show(x + y))
}
```

**Simple rule: See `{` -> one `let` per line, no `in`. See `=` -> use `in`.**
**Multi-statement `match` arms and `if`/`else` branches** work either wrapped in `{ ... }` (canonical `ailang fmt` form) or as unbraced `let ...; ...` / newline-separated statements:
```ailang
-- ✅ Multi-statement match arm and if branch
pure func adjust(opt: Option[int], flag: bool) -> int =
  match opt {
    Some(x) => {
      let doubled = x * 2
      if flag then {
        let bumped = doubled + 1
        bumped
      } else doubled
    },
    None => 0
  }
```

## Function Calls: Multi-arg vs Curried (CRITICAL)

**Two styles with DIFFERENT call syntax:**

```ailang
-- MULTI-ARG FUNC: Call with commas f(a, b)
func add(a: int, b: int) -> int = a + b
let result1 = add(3, 4)     -- CORRECT: 7
-- let bad = add(3)(4)      -- WRONG: arity mismatch!

-- CURRIED LAMBDA: Call with chained f(a)(b)
let addC = \a. \b. a + b
let result2 = addC(3)(4)    -- CORRECT: 7
let add10 = addC(10)        -- Partial application!
-- let bad = addC(3, 4)     -- WRONG: arity mismatch!
```

**Rule: Match call style to definition style:**
| Definition | Call Style | Partial App? |
|------------|------------|--------------|
| `func f(a, b) = ...` | `f(a, b)` | No |
| `let f = \a. \b. ...` | `f(a)(b)` | Yes |

**Higher-order with curried lambdas:**
```ailang
module benchmark/solution
import std/io (println)

export func main() -> () ! {IO} {
  let compose = \f. \g. \x. f(g(x));
  let double = \x. x * 2;
  let addOne = \x. x + 1;
  let doubleThenAdd = compose(addOne)(double);  -- Curried: chain calls
  println(show(doubleThenAdd(5)))
}
```

**Using std/list foldl (IMPORTANT - use inline func syntax!):**
```ailang
module benchmark/solution
import std/io (println)
import std/list (foldl)

-- std/list foldl signature: foldl(f: (acc, elem) -> acc, initial, list)
-- RECOMMENDED: Use inline func syntax for reliable type inference

export func main() -> () ! {IO} {
  -- MOST RELIABLE: inline func with explicit types
  let sum = foldl(func(acc: int, x: int) -> int { acc + x }, 0, [1,2,3,4,5]);
  println(show(sum))
}
```

**foldl syntax options:**
```ailang
import std/list (foldl)

pure func sumOptions(xs: [int]) -> (int, int, int) {
  -- RECOMMENDED: space-separated multi-param lambda (concise)
  let a = foldl(\acc x. acc + x, 0, xs)
  -- VERBOSE: inline func with explicit types (also works)
  let b = foldl(func(acc: int, x: int) -> int { acc + x }, 0, xs)
  -- ALSO WORKS: curried lambda (longer; prefer the multi-param form)
  let c = foldl(\acc. \x. acc + x, 0, xs);
  (a, b, c)
}
```

**For callbacks passed to `foldl`, `sortBy`, `zipWith`, `foldlE`, etc., write `\a b. body`**
(one lambda, several params): it is the simplest form. Curried `\a. \b. body` also works.
Irrefutable tuple and record destructuring work directly in lambda parameters (`\(k, v). ...`, `\acc (k, v). acc + v`, `\{ age, ... }. age`).

**Pipe operator (`|>`):** `x |> f` passes `x` to **unary** function `f` (left-associative, lowest precedence). Wrap multi-arg calls or inline lambdas in parens (e.g. `opt |> (\v. getOrElse(v, 0))`):
```ailang
import std/list (filter, map)

pure func pipeDemo(xs: [int]) -> [int] =
  xs |> (\ys. filter(\x. x > 0, ys)) |> (\ys. map(\x. x * 2, ys))
```

**Sorting with sortBy:**
```ailang
import std/list (sortBy)

-- Comparator returns: negative if a < b, 0 if equal, positive if a > b
func cmpInt(a: int, b: int) -> int = a - b

let sorted = sortBy(cmpInt, [3, 1, 4, 1, 5])  -- [1, 1, 3, 4, 5]

-- Reverse sort: swap arguments
func cmpDesc(a: int, b: int) -> int = b - a
let descending = sortBy(cmpDesc, [3, 1, 4])   -- [4, 3, 1]
```

## Recursive Lambdas (letrec)

**Use `letrec` when a lambda needs to call itself:**

```ailang
module benchmark/solution

export func main() -> () ! {IO} {
  -- WRONG: `let` for self-referential lambda
  -- let factorial = \n. if n <= 1 then 1 else n * factorial(n - 1);  -- ERROR: undefined 'factorial'

  -- RIGHT: use `letrec` for recursive lambdas
  letrec factorial = \n. if n <= 1 then 1 else n * factorial(n - 1);
  println(show(factorial(5)))  -- 120
}
```

**When to use `letrec` vs `func`:**
| Case | Use |
|------|-----|
| Top-level recursive function | `func f(...) = ...` (preferred) |
| Recursive lambda inside block | `letrec f = \x. ... f(...)` |
| Non-recursive lambda | `let f = \x. ...` |

**Mutual recursion: use top-level `func` declarations** (last example below). Two local
`letrec`s cannot see each other: `letrec isEven = ...isOdd(n - 1)` followed by `letrec isOdd = ...`
fails with `undefined variable: isOdd`, and `letrec a = ..., b = ...` does not parse.

**Where to put a `letrec`:** it needs a statement sequence, and both a `{...}`
block body and a `= ...` equation body give it one. Prefer the block — it is what
`ailang fmt` emits, so formatting will not rewrite what you wrote.

```ailang
-- ✅ PREFERRED: `{ ... }` block; the `;` separates statements
export func is_even(n: int) -> bool {
  letrec is_odd = \m. if m == 0 then false else is_even(m - 1);
  if n == 0 then true else is_odd(n - 1)
}
```
```ailang
-- ✅ BEST for mutual recursion: top-level `func` declarations
func is_odd(n: int) -> bool =
  if n == 0 then false else is_even(n - 1)

export func is_even(n: int) -> bool =
  if n == 0 then true else is_odd(n - 1)
```

## Type Annotations for Higher-Order Functions

**Annotate function types with parentheses around arrow types:**

```ailang
-- Single-argument function type
let double: int -> int = \x. x * 2

-- Higher-order: function taking a function
let apply: (int -> int) -> int -> int = \f. \x. f(x)

-- Multiple function parameters
let compose: (int -> int) -> (int -> int) -> int -> int = \f. \g. \x. f(g(x))
```

**Type annotation on multi-arg named function:**
```ailang
func twice(f: int -> int, x: int) -> int = f(f(x))
```

## Syntax Reference

| Construct | Syntax |
|-----------|--------|
| Module | `module path/name` |
| Import | `import std/io (println)` |
| Import alias | `import std/list as L` |
| Function | `export func name(x: int) -> int ! {IO} { body }` |
| Lambda | `\x. x * 2` |
| Recursive lambda | `letrec f = \x. ... f(x) ...` |
| Pattern match | `match x { 0 => a, n => b }` (use `=>`, commas between arms) |
| ADT | `type Tree = Leaf(int) \| Node(Tree, int, Tree)` |
| ADT with Eq | `type Color = Red \| Green \| Blue deriving (Eq)` |
| Record with Eq | `type Point = {x: int, y: int} deriving (Eq)` (anonymous records have no `==`) |
| `deriving (Json)` | `type Cfg = { host: string, tag: Option[string] } deriving (Eq, Json)` synthesizes pure `encodeCfg(v: Cfg) -> Json` & `decodeCfg(j: Json) -> Result[Cfg, string]` (requires `import std/json (Json)`; `Option` fields omit `None` on encode and accept missing/`null` on decode; ADTs use `{"tag": ...}`) |
| `let` `?` propagation | `let x = expr?` (or `let (a, b) = expr?`) unwraps `Ok`/`Some` on the return spine of `Result[_, E]` / `Option[_]` functions and early-returns `Err`/`None` (let-bound only; hoist sub-expressions) |
| `==` / `!=` support | int, float, string, bool, and any list, `Option`, `Result` or tuple whose parts support it (`xs == []`, `o == Some(3)`, `(a, b) == (1, "x")`), plus types declared `deriving (Eq)`. Functions have no `==`. Float `==` is IEEE: NaN is never equal to anything, itself included; test with `isNaN(x)` from `std/math`. Float `<` `<=` `>` `>=` are IEEE too: false whenever either side is NaN, so `if x > hi` does not catch a NaN |
| Record | `{name: "A", age: 30}` |
| Record update | `{base \| field: val}` |
| Open record type | `{name: string \| r}` or `{name: string, ...}` |
| List cons | `x :: xs` or `::(x, xs)` |
| Array literal | `#[1, 2, 3]` |
| Pipe operator | `x \|> f \|> g` (left-associative, passes `x` to unary `f`) |
| Typed hole | `_?` or `?name` (fails check with `TC_HOLE`: expected type + in-scope locals) |
| Effect | `! {IO, FS, Net}` after return type |

## Effects (Side Effects Must Be Declared)

**Every function performing I/O must declare effects in the signature!**

Calling a function-valued record field performs its annotated effects. Passing a
function to a higher-order function with an unannotated or effect-polymorphic
callback parameter also requires the caller to declare the callback’s effects.
This includes a function stored in a list, tuple, Option or record argument.
Constructing a record that stores a callback does not perform those effects.

Callback **function types** distinguish these contracts:

| Callback type | Contract |
|---|---|
| `T -> U` | Implicit open row; hand-off charges the caller, including nested callback data |
| `T -> U ! {}` | Closed pure callback; an effectful value is rejected even if its caller declares that effect |
| `T -> U ! {IO}` | Concrete IO callback contract; the callee declares IO when it invokes it |
| `T -> U ! {e}` | Explicit row polymorphism; share `e` with the enclosing caller row |

For a store-only helper taking a mixed record of pure and effectful callbacks,
write `! {}` on pure callback fields and concrete rows on effectful fields.
Direct record/list/tuple literals still only store callback values.


```ailang
import std/io (println, readLine, exit)
import std/fs (readFile)
import std/net (httpGet)
import std/env (getArgs)

-- Pure (no effects) - use `pure func` or omit effect annotation.
-- `pure` means `! {}`: `pure func f() -> () ! {IO}` is a type error (drop `pure` or the row).
pure func add(x: int, y: int) -> int = x + y

-- IO effect - for print/println/readLine
func greet(name: string) -> () ! {IO} = println("Hello ${name}")

-- Single effect with return value
func ask(prompt: string) -> string ! {IO} {
  println(prompt);
  readLine()
}

-- Multiple effects
func process(path: string) -> () ! {IO, FS} {
  let content = readFile(path);
  println(content)
}

-- Main function typically needs effects
func mainHello() -> () ! {IO} {
  println("Hello, World!")
}

-- Exit with explicit code (for CLI tools)
func mainExit() -> () ! {IO} {
  println("error: invalid argument");
  exit(1)
}

-- Main with file system access
func mainFS() -> () ! {IO, FS} {
  let content = readFile("data.txt");
  println(content)
}

-- Main with network
func mainNet() -> () ! {IO, Net} {
  let body = httpGet("https://example.com");
  println(body)
}

-- Main with CLI arguments (getArgs returns [string], needs Env)
-- Run: ailang run --caps IO,FS,Env --entry main program.ail -- arg1 arg2
func mainArgs() -> () ! {IO, FS, Env} {
  let args = getArgs();
  match args {
    filename :: _ => {
      let content = readFile(filename);
      println(content)
    },
    _ => println("Usage: program <filename>")
  }
}

-- Reading lines from stdin (readLine reads one line, returns "" at EOF)
-- Run: printf "hello\nworld\n" | ailang run --caps IO --entry main program.ail
func loop() -> () ! {IO} {
  let line = readLine();
  if line == "" then ()
  else {
    println("Got: ${line}");
    loop()
  }
}
```

**Common effect combinations:**
| Task | Required Effects |
|------|------------------|
| Print output | `! {IO}` |
| Read files | `! {FS}` (add IO if also printing) |
| HTTP requests | `! {Net}` (add IO if also printing) |
| Environment vars | `! {Env}` |
| CLI arguments | `! {Env}` (use `getArgs()` from `std/env`) |
| Read from stdin | `! {IO}` (use `readLine()` from `std/io`) |
| AI calls | `! {AI}` |
| Run external commands | `! {Process}` or `! {IO, Process}` |
| Exit with code | `! {IO}` (use `exit(code)` from `std/io`) |
| Full program | `! {IO, FS, Net}` as needed |

**Effect errors and how to fix:**
```
Error: Effect checking failed for function 'main'
  Function uses effects not declared in signature
  Missing effects: IO
```

**Fix:** Add the missing effect to your function signature:
```not-ailang
-- WRONG: missing IO effect
export func main() -> () { println("hi") }
```
```ailang
module examples/io_fix

-- CORRECT: declare IO effect
export func main() -> () ! {IO} { println("hi") }
```

| Effect | Functions | Import |
|--------|-----------|--------|
